name: Alcántara Bridge
scope: Whole surviving Roman bridge across the Tagus at Alcántara, Cáceres: all six unequal round through-vaults, five tall piers with native rectangular/pointed cutwater projections and stepped base ledges, both abutments/approach-wing masonry, narrow paved stone deck and solid parapets, intrinsic central triumphal gateway with an open arched road passage, cornices/attic and bounded inscription-panel recesses. Exclude the separate Roman temple outside the bridge footprint on the southeast approach, Torre del Oro/town walls, downstream modern viaduct/dam, natural river/water/bedrock/hills/trees and whole valley/approach road slabs. This is the whole bridge and its attached honorific arch, not a complete model of every building in the surrounding monument complex.
era: Surviving six-arch bridge and central honorific gateway. Exact Qualla-published circa1870Laurent photograph controls permanent stone architecture after1860restoration; current town authority confirms all six spans/five piers/granite masonry/central honorific arch. Fine present conservation patches/parapet inscriptions and partly submerged foundation/riverbed grades not surveyed, no intact Roman-era reconstruction.
